scope: Theorem 9.7 (Finite passage templates) of the manuscript “Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles” (preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ff8e55372a94e4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 128. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each degree bound d, there is a finite collection of scalar identity pieces, coordinate charts and passage rules, and integers Nd, Ed, with the following properties. 1. On the square, every polynomial field of degree at most d has the stated finite globally subanalytic subdivision. Its interior scalar fields are constant-state fields, nozero or simple-root boxes of Equation (9.9), or monomial annuli of Equation (9.6). Their analytic factors have uniform larger neighborhoods and their nonconstant arguments have the prescribed fixed smallness. All changes back to physical coordinates use parameter-only data, positive rational powers, and bounded analytic operations. 2. The further real passage refinements in Section 10 are finite; in particular Lemma 9.5 allows at most one weighted redo at a nonzero generator resonance. 3. Apart from at most Ed periodic orbits containing tangential boundary arcs, every periodic orbit is a cyclic concatenation of at most Nd interior passages and physical graph connectors. There are only finitely many resulting words, including all choices of chart, sign, orientation, and the finitely many endpoint passage rules. The choices and bounds include all coefficient degeneracies.
